labels.definition: Vaccines themselves: specific vaccines, the childhood schedule, mandates and exemptions, efficacy, ingredients, and alleged adverse effects. Apply to vaccine content whatever the stance; conspiracy or distrust framing is coded separately on the frame axis.
labels.name: Vaccines & Immunization

labels.definition: SARS-CoV-2 infection, long COVID, pandemic-era measures and policies, and COVID treatments. COVID vaccines belong to Vaccines & Immunization unless the subject is the disease, the pandemic response, or its origin.
labels.name: COVID-19 / Pandemic Health

labels.definition: Outbreaks, transmission and surveillance of infectious diseases other than COVID, including preparedness. Routine immunisation against them goes to Vaccines & Immunization.
labels.name: Infectious-Disease Outbreaks

labels.definition: Female reproductive endocrinology and conditions across the life course, including menopause and hormone therapy. Pregnancy and postpartum go to Pregnancy / Maternal / Postpartum Health; contraception, abortion and fertility treatment to Reproductive & Sexual Health.
labels.name: Women’s Health & Female Hormones

labels.definition: Conception onward: pregnancy, birth, the postpartum period, infant feeding, and medications or exposures during pregnancy. Fertility treatment and abortion go to Reproductive & Sexual Health.
labels.name: Pregnancy / Maternal / Postpartum Health

labels.definition: Contraception, abortion, fertility treatment, sexually transmitted infection and sexual function. Menopausal hormone therapy goes to Women’s Health & Female Hormones.
labels.name: Reproductive & Sexual Health

labels.definition: Health care and health disparities specific to LGBTQ+ people, including gender-affirming care. Legislative or regulatory debate about that care may additionally take Public-Health Policy.
labels.name: LGBTQ+/Gender Health

labels.definition: Male reproductive and hormonal health, testosterone therapy, prostate and sexual function, and hair loss. Compounds used to build muscle or performance go to Performance-Enhancing Drugs; subcultural masculinity practices to Manosphere.
labels.name: Men’s Health & Male Hormones

labels.definition: Health and body practices drawn from online masculinity subcultures, and their vocabulary. Clinical testosterone or fertility content goes to Men’s Health & Male Hormones.
labels.name: Manosphere / Masculinity-Adjacent Health

labels.definition: Body weight, dieting for weight loss, obesity, and metabolic dysfunction discussed as a weight or lifestyle matter. Clinical cardiovascular and diabetes markers and their drugs go to Cardiometabolic Health.
labels.name: Weight Loss & Metabolic Health

labels.definition: GLP-1 and related incretin drugs specifically: named products, dosing, side effects, compounding, and products marketed as natural substitutes for them.
labels.name: GLP-1 / Incretin Drugs

labels.definition: Research peptides and growth-hormone secretagogues used for recovery, fat loss, cognition or longevity. Anabolic steroids and SARMs go to Performance-Enhancing Drugs; incretin peptides to GLP-1 / Incretin Drugs.
labels.name: Peptides / Experimental Optimization Compounds

labels.definition: Anabolic steroids, SARMs, growth hormone and cycling protocols used to build muscle or athletic performance. Peptides used for recovery or longevity rather than performance go to Peptides.
labels.name: Performance-Enhancing Drugs / Bodybuilding Compounds

labels.definition: Exercise itself: modality, dose, programming, technique and fitness metrics. Post-exercise recovery modalities go to Recovery & Physical Optimization.
labels.name: Fitness & Exercise

labels.definition: Modalities used to recover or feel better physically — heat, cold, compression, light, bodywork, mobility work. The systematic-optimisation framing around them is coded on the frame axis, not here.
labels.name: Recovery & Physical Optimization

labels.definition: Sleep quality, duration, timing and disorders, and the practices and products sold to improve them. Fatigue attributed to a named chronic illness goes to Chronic / Complex Symptom Communities.
labels.name: Sleep

labels.definition: Stress physiology and the popular nervous-system-regulation vocabulary: cortisol talk, vagus nerve, breathwork, somatic practice, burnout. Diagnosed anxiety, trauma or mood disorders go to Mental Health.
labels.name: Stress / Nervous-System Regulation / Neurowellness

labels.definition: Psychiatric conditions, their diagnosis and treatment, therapy, and popular psychology vocabulary. Cortisol and nervous-system framing goes to Stress / Nervous-System Regulation.
labels.name: Mental Health

labels.definition: Cognitive performance, focus, memory, dementia prevention, and the substances or routines aimed at them. Psychiatric conditions go to Mental Health.
labels.name: Brain / Cognition / Productivity

labels.definition: Foods, nutrients, additives and the health effects attributed to them. A named dietary pattern or identity goes to Diet Tribes; pills, powders and nutraceuticals to Functional Nutrition & Supplements.
labels.name: Food & Nutrition

labels.definition: Named dietary patterns and the identities and arguments around them. Discussion of a single food or nutrient on its merits goes to Food & Nutrition.
labels.name: Diet Tribes / Food Ideologies

labels.definition: Supplements, powders and nutraceuticals: what is in them, what they are claimed to do, and how they are sold. Nutrients as eaten in food go to Food & Nutrition.
labels.name: Functional Nutrition & Supplements

labels.definition: The gut microbiome, digestive symptoms and conditions, and the testing and products aimed at them.
labels.name: Gut Health / Microbiome

labels.definition: Inflammation invoked as a general explanation of disease, or as a property of foods and lifestyles. Diagnosed autoimmune disease goes to Autoimmune / Immune Health.
labels.name: Inflammation as a General Health Narrative

labels.definition: Alternative, integrative and complementary systems of care and their practitioners. Apply when a modality or practice is actually discussed; the anti-mainstream rhetoric that often accompanies it is a separate frame label.
labels.name: Natural / Alternative / Functional Medicine

labels.definition: Detox, cleanse and antiparasitic protocols as practices — what to take, how and why. General toxin or parasite rhetoric with no protocol is a frame label, not this topic.
labels.name: Detox / Cleanses / Parasites

labels.definition: Non-standard cancer treatments and narratives about alternative or suppressed cures, including chemotherapy refusal.
labels.name: Cancer Alternative Treatments / Cure Narratives

labels.definition: Skin, hair and cosmetic concerns and the topical products and procedures aimed at them. Injectable regenerative procedures go to Regenerative / Aesthetic Medicine.
labels.name: Beauty / Dermatology / Skincare

labels.definition: Platelet, stem-cell, exosome and related regenerative injections for aesthetic or orthopaedic use. Topical skincare and standard dermatology go to Beauty / Dermatology / Skincare.
labels.name: Regenerative / Aesthetic Medicine

labels.definition: Lifespan and healthspan extension: biological-age testing, longevity drugs, clinics and protocols aimed explicitly at ageing. General self-optimisation with no longevity goal goes to Biohacking / Human Optimization.
labels.name: Longevity / Anti-Aging

labels.definition: Self-experimentation and systematic self-optimisation as a practice and identity. Where a specific modality is the real subject, prefer that topic and code the framing on the frame axis.
labels.name: Biohacking / Human Optimization

labels.definition: Devices, at-home tests and apps used to measure the body, and the interpretation of what they report.
labels.name: Wearables / Self-Tracking / Digital Health

labels.definition: AI systems used for health advice, diagnosis, therapy or content, and their reliability.
labels.name: AI & Health Information

labels.definition: Dependence, overdose, treatment, recovery and harm reduction for drugs of misuse. Cannabis and psychedelics, nicotine and caffeine, and alcohol each have their own topic.
labels.name: Substance Use / Addiction / Harm Reduction

labels.definition: Cannabis, psychedelics and adjacent substances, including therapeutic use, microdosing and legal status.
labels.name: Cannabis / Psychedelics / Emerging Psychoactive Substances

labels.definition: Nicotine and caffeine products and their claimed cognitive or performance benefits.
labels.name: Nicotine / Tobacco / Stimulants

labels.definition: Alcohol’s health effects, drinking norms, sobriety culture and alcohol alternatives.
labels.name: Alcohol / Sober Wellness

labels.definition: Health effects attributed to named environmental and chemical exposures. Fluoride goes to Fluoride / Oral Health and radiofrequency to EMF / Technology Exposure; unspecified toxic-load rhetoric is a frame label.
labels.name: Environmental Health / Chemical Exposures

labels.definition: Teeth, gums, the oral microbiome, and fluoride in water and dental products.
labels.name: Fluoride / Oral Health

labels.definition: Health effects attributed to electromagnetic fields, wireless technology, and screen or blue-light exposure.
labels.name: EMF / Technology Exposure

labels.definition: Health of infants, children and adolescents, and the products, medications and exposures specific to them. Autism causation goes to Neurodevelopment / Autism Discourse; the childhood vaccine schedule to Vaccines & Immunization.
labels.name: Children’s Health

labels.definition: Autism and neurodevelopmental conditions: causes, prevalence, treatment and cure claims, and the debate around them.
labels.name: Neurodevelopment / Autism Discourse

labels.definition: Contested, overlapping or hard-to-diagnose chronic-symptom conditions and the patient communities around them.
labels.name: Chronic / Complex Symptom Communities

labels.definition: Immune function and diagnosed autoimmune disease, including diets and protocols aimed at them. Inflammation as a general explanatory narrative goes to Inflammation as a General Health Narrative.
labels.name: Autoimmune / Immune Health

labels.definition: Cardiovascular and metabolic disease and its clinical markers and drugs: blood pressure, lipids, ApoB, statins, diabetes, fatty liver. Weight and dieting as such go to Weight Loss & Metabolic Health.
labels.name: Cardiometabolic Health

labels.definition: Musculoskeletal pain and injury and their treatment, including manual therapy and rehabilitation.
labels.name: Pain / Musculoskeletal Health

labels.definition: Medicine’s institutions, costs, incentives, regulators and trustworthiness discussed as a subject. Distrust expressed as rhetoric rather than discussed as a subject is coded on the frame axis.
labels.name: Health-Care System / Medical Trust

labels.definition: Government and institutional health policy: mandates, regulation, guidelines, funding and their politics.
labels.name: Public-Health Policy

labels.definition: The Make America Healthy Again movement as a subject: its agenda, figures, programme and politics. MAHA-style rhetoric is coded on the frame axis; use this topic when the movement itself is what is being discussed.
labels.name: MAHA / “Root Cause” Health Politics

labels.definition: Cancer as a disease: risk factors, screening, diagnosis, staging, and conventional treatment such as chemotherapy, radiation and surgery. Suppressed-cure and cancer-conspiracy rhetoric is coded on the frame axis; alternative cancer remedies go to Natural & Traditional Medicine.
labels.name: Cancer

labels.definition: Conditions of the brain and nervous system and how they present: seizures and epilepsy, brain tumours, concussion, stroke, migraine, and neurological difference described as a condition. Mental-health conditions go to Mental Health; cognitive optimisation goes to Brain / Cognition / Productivity.
labels.name: Neurology / Seizures / Brain Conditions

labels.definition: Age-related cognitive decline and the conditions and care around it. Longevity and anti-ageing protocols go to Longevity / Anti-Ageing.
labels.name: Dementia / Cognitive Decline / Ageing

labels.definition: Acute injury and what is done about it: wounds, burns, fractures, bites, infection of a wound, first aid and urgent care. Chronic musculoskeletal pain goes to Pain / Musculoskeletal Health.
labels.name: Injury / Wound Care / First Aid

labels.definition: Operations and clinical procedures, the hospital experience around them, and recovery from them.
labels.name: Surgery / Medical Procedures

labels.definition: The senses and their loss, correction and aids.
labels.name: Hearing / Vision / Sensory Health

labels.definition: Heredity and genetic explanation: what is inherited, how traits and blood types pass on, genetic testing and conditions with a genetic cause.
labels.name: Genetics / Inheritance

concepts: name the subject in the summary
labels.definition: Substantive health, medicine or wellness content that no other topic label fits. Name the subject in the summary. Never use it as a second-choice label when a listed topic applies — it exists to make gaps in the taxonomy visible.
labels.name: Other health topic

labels.definition: A study, trial or research literature is invoked as support for a point. Applies whether or not the study is named, real or correctly described.
labels.name: Scientific-study citation

labels.definition: A prestigious institution, journal or affiliation is named to lend authority, rather than a specific finding being discussed on its content.
labels.name: Prestige-science invocation

labels.definition: Biological mechanism vocabulary is used to explain a claim or make it sound plausible, without a study being cited.
labels.name: Mechanistic/scientific language

labels.definition: An explicit assertion about how well established something is: proven, clinically proven, science-backed, evidence-based, FDA approved.
labels.name: Evidence-strength claim

labels.definition: The evidence actually offered is preliminary, indirect or anecdotal — animal or cell studies, observational association, preprints, single cases. Code the evidence the speaker offers, not your judgement of whether their conclusion is warranted.
labels.name: Weak-evidence / extrapolation signal

labels.definition: Personal or second-hand experience is offered as grounds for a general conclusion. Apply only where experience functions as evidence, not to every anecdote.
labels.name: Personal-experience evidence

labels.definition: A person’s title, training or professional identity is invoked as grounds for believing a claim.
labels.name: Credential appeal

labels.definition: Conventional medicine or ordinary doctors are portrayed as ignorant, captured, or unable to help. Discussing the health system as a subject is the Health-Care System topic; this label is for the rhetoric.
labels.name: Anti-mainstream-medicine framing

labels.definition: Research, treatments or information are described as hidden, censored, buried or suppressed.
labels.name: Suppressed-science framing

labels.definition: A finding, guideline, institution or person is discounted because of who funds, employs or profits from them.
labels.name: Conflict-of-interest framing

labels.definition: The pharmaceutical industry is cast as a self-interested actor shaping medicine against patients’ interests.
labels.name: Big Pharma / medical-industrial complex

labels.definition: The food industry is cast as deliberately or negligently harming health. An allegation that the food supply is intentionally poisoned goes to Food conspiracy.
labels.name: Big Food / food-system distrust

labels.definition: Public agencies, regulators or official science are portrayed as corrupt, lying or not to be trusted.
labels.name: Government/institution distrust

labels.definition: Health decisions are framed in terms of autonomy, informed consent, parental rights or freedom from mandate.
labels.name: Medical freedom

labels.definition: Something is recommended or condemned on the grounds of being natural, ancestral, traditional, clean or chemical-free.
labels.name: Naturalness appeal

labels.definition: Getting to an underlying cause is contrasted with merely treating symptoms, or reversal is promised in place of management.
labels.name: Root-cause framing

labels.definition: Health problems are attributed to accumulated toxins or chemical burden in general terms. A named exposure discussed on its evidence is the Environmental Health topic.
labels.name: Toxin framing

labels.definition: Moral or aesthetic clean-versus-dirty, pure-versus-poisoned language applied to foods, products or bodies.
labels.name: Purity/contamination framing

labels.definition: A coordinated, hidden and malign effort is alleged. Requires an actual allegation of coordination or concealment; criticism, distrust or incompetence alone is not enough.
labels.name: Conspiracy/cover-up

labels.definition: Conspiracy narratives specific to COVID, its origin, its response, or COVID vaccines.
labels.name: COVID conspiracy

labels.definition: Conspiracy narratives about weather, the sky, geoengineering or ambient radiation.
labels.name: Geo/environment conspiracy

labels.definition: Conspiracy narratives about hidden or suppressed cancer cures and the motives of cancer medicine.
labels.name: Cancer conspiracy

labels.definition: The food supply is alleged to be deliberately engineered to harm. Ordinary criticism of industry practice goes to Big Food / food-system distrust.
labels.name: Food conspiracy

labels.definition: Conspiracy narratives about deliberate harm through fluoridation. Discussion of fluoride evidence or policy on its merits is the Fluoride / Oral Health topic.
labels.name: Fluoride conspiracy

labels.definition: Parasites are offered as a general explanation for chronic illness, or deworming as routine health maintenance.
labels.name: Parasite framework

labels.definition: The movement’s own framing: a childhood chronic-disease crisis with dietary and environmental root causes. Requires that framing, not merely a mention of one of its concerns.
labels.name: MAHA – official/core vocabulary

labels.definition: MAHA-style framing of the food supply — ultra-processed food, dyes, additives, real food, school food. Do not apply merely because such a food is mentioned; the movement’s framing must be present.
labels.name: MAHA – food vocabulary

labels.definition: MAHA-style framing of pesticide and chemical exposure as a driver of chronic disease. Ordinary discussion of an exposure is the Environmental Health topic.
labels.name: MAHA – environmental vocabulary

labels.definition: The online shorthand cluster that signals alignment without the movement’s formal vocabulary: seed oils, fluoride, medical freedom, vaccine injury, corporate capture.
labels.name: MAHA-adjacent online vocabulary

labels.definition: Health is framed as a performance problem to be maximised, with protocols, stacks, targets and peak states.
labels.name: Optimization framing

labels.definition: Self-experimentation framing specifically: n-of-1 trials, stacks, protocols, quantified routines.
labels.name: Biohacking framing

labels.definition: The passage sells or monetises: sponsorship, discount codes, affiliate links, or the speaker’s own product, clinic, programme or book. Applies to a host’s own products as well as paid reads; set relevance to advertisement only inside a delimited ad break.
labels.name: Commercialization

labels.definition: Ordinary judgement, lived experience or independent research is elevated over expertise and credentialed authority.
labels.name: Anti-expert / populist framing

labels.definition: The speaker corrects, fact-checks or debunks a health claim. Apply regardless of whether the correction is itself accurate.
labels.name: Misinformation correction / debunking
